**Ruled out:**
- **Origin / load balancer:** the origin is a Layer-4 NLB (TCP:80) — architecturally incapable of emitting HTTP 403; no HTTP metrics, no access logs.
- **Other WAF rules:** AntiDDoS, IP reputation, KnownBadInputs, SQLi, and the Count-only rate-based rule all contributed **zero** blocks.
- **Config/permission changes in AWS:** no WAFv2, CloudFront, IAM, S3, Glue, or Athena mutations in CloudTrail.

**Investigation gaps (both tie back to the "no-athena-permission" label):**
1. **Raw WAF logs unreadable** — the agent role was denied `s3:GetObject` on `aws-waf-logs-012345678901_1` and all `athena:*` actions on the configured `default.waf_logs` Glue table. This is the "no Athena permission" condition. It prevents request-level attribution (source IPs, URIs, HTTP methods), so I **cannot confirm whether the blocked traffic was a malicious burst (WAF working as intended) or legitimate traffic being false-positived.** Granting read access (`s3:GetObject` on the log bucket, or Athena query permissions + results-location access) would close this.
2. **EKS UI pod logs unreachable** — kubectl denied (cluster `example-shop` uses `CONFIG_MAP` auth, agent role not in `aws-auth`; no CloudWatch log group holds UI stdout). Does not affect the WAF conclusion, but means any separate application-level behavior can't be observed from here.

**Bottom line for the user:** Yes — AWS WAF is involved, and it is the direct and sole source of the observed 403 responses. The specific culprit is the AWS Managed Common Rule Set (`SizeRestrictions_BODY` then `NoUserAgent_HEADER`) on web ACL `CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4`, blocking a traffic pattern that appeared at 17:30 and faded by 18:30. The one open question — whether that traffic was abusive or legitimate — can't be answered without the raw WAF log read permissions the agent currently lacks.

I already engaged the mitigation specialist with this single actionable cause (the CommonRuleSet blocking on `CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4`), including the Athena/S3 log-read permission gap and the recommended scoped, reversible options. The subsequent findings (EKS log access gap) added no new or distinct actionable cause, so I am not re-engaging it — it already has the complete, current picture.", "type": "text"}], "user_reference": null}

The mitigation proposal addresses this appropriately: a surgical, reversible `RuleActionOverrides`-to-Count on just the two implicated CRS sub-rules, **gated** behind first obtaining the WAF-log read access to confirm the traffic is legitimate before loosening protection. # Investigation Summary

## Symptoms

### HTTP 403s on CloudFront d111111abcdef8 (EEXAMPLE000001)
**Description:** A subset of customers and automated clients received HTTP 403 on the example-shop UI distribution during 17:30–18:30 UTC on 2026-10-06. CloudFront 4xxErrorRate rose from ~0% baseline to a 2.54% peak and returned to 0% by 18:30; request throughput held steady (~11k req/5min), so these were per-request rejections, not an outage. Self-recovered by 18:30.
**Time:** 2026-10-06T17:30:00Z - 2026-10-06T18:30:00Z

## Findings

### Root Cause: WAF Common Rule Set blocked ~1,799 requests, returning the 403s
**Description:** The attached web ACL `CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4` blocked ~1,799 requests via `AWS-AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet` (priority 3), 100% of all blocks. Two phases: `SizeRestrictions_BODY` ~1,200 blocks (17:30–17:50, oversized request bodies) and `NoUserAgent_HEADER` ~599 blocks (18:05–18:25, missing User-Agent, consistent with automated clients). WAF BLOCK returns HTTP 403; onset, the 17:55–18:00 dip, and 18:30 recovery align exactly with the CloudFront 4xx spike, and 0 blocks across the 16:00–17:25 baseline. Because CloudTrail shows no WAF/CloudFront/IAM config change, the rules were already enforcing — the fundamental trigger was an input/traffic change at 17:30 (clients began sending requests that trip these CRS checks), which fixing the recurring input would stop. AntiDDoS, IpReputation, KnownBadInputs, SQLi, and the Count-only rate-based rule contributed zero blocks.
**Cascades to:** symptom-cf-403

#### Gaps
- **Raw WAF logs unreadable — no request-level attribution (the “no-athena-permission” condition):** The agent role was denied s3:GetObject on aws-waf-logs-012345678901_1 and all athena:* actions (StartQueryExecution/GetQueryExecution) on the configured default.waf_logs Glue table. The logs exist and are listable, and the table is configured — only read permission is missing. Consequence: per-request fields (clientIp, URI, HTTP method, country, blocked samples) are unavailable, so whether the blocked traffic was a malicious burst (WAF working as intended) or legitimate traffic being false-positived cannot be confirmed. Unblock: grant s3:GetObject on the log bucket, or athena:StartQueryExecution/GetQueryExecution/GetQueryResults plus s3:GetObject on the Athena results location.
- **EKS UI pod logs unreachable — fundamental trigger unconfirmable:** The originating client/workload behind the 17:30 input-shape change cannot be identified: kubectl is denied (cluster example-shop uses CONFIG_MAP auth and the agent role DevOpsAgentRole-AgentSpace-74267d73f77b is not in aws-auth), no CloudWatch log group holds UI stdout (only /aws/eks/example-shop/cluster control-plane logs; Application Signals empty for the window), and no ui-namespace IRSA role is enumerable (UI likely uses the node instance role). This does NOT weaken the WAF conclusion — WAF-blocked requests never reach the origin. Unblock: map the agent role into the example-shop aws-auth ConfigMap (or enable API access entries) with read on namespace ui.

# Mitigation Summary

## Action
Set RuleActionOverrides to Count for the two implicated sub-rules — SizeRestrictions_BODY and NoUserAgent_HEADER — within AWS-AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet (priority 3) of web ACL CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4, keeping every other sub-rule and rule group in BLOCK. Fully reversible. Prerequisite: grant the monitoring role read access to the already-enabled WAF logs so request-level attribution can confirm malicious vs. legitimate before the override is made permanent.

## Reasoning
During 17:30–18:30 UTC on 2026-10-06, web ACL CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 blocked 1,799 requests — 100% from AWS-AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet in BLOCK mode (SizeRestrictions_BODY ~1,200, NoUserAgent_HEADER ~599). No config change caused it; a traffic/input change triggered the already-enforcing rules and the incident self-recovered. The config is unchanged, so recurrence is possible. CAVEAT: it is NOT confirmed whether the blocked traffic was malicious (keep BLOCK) or legitimate false-positives (relax), because the monitoring role lacks WAF-log read access. The change is deliberately surgical, reversible, and gated behind attribution.

```
**Purpose:** Persist the complete current web ACL (full Rules array + LockToken) as the authoritative rollback baseline before any change; the Common Rule Set rule in it must have no RuleActionOverrides.
**Advisory:** Confirm the saved file is the exact web ACL being modified (Id f0598f76-f04d-456a-beff-5521b48914d4, Scope CLOUDFRONT) before relying on it for rollback.

```
